subject: Workspace provisioning & initial access plan — Blueharbor Analytics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anthony Ruiz <anthony.ruiz@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Workspace provisioning & initial access plan — Blueharbor Analytics

Hi Anthony / Clara,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum, I put together a short, actionable plan for the first-week provisioning of your Redwood workspace and API access. The objective is to get a secure dev sandbox and a production workspace with scoped API tokens so your engineering team can start integration testing next week.

Top-level plan (high level):
- Create two workspaces: blueharbor-dev and blueharbor-prod.
- Seed one admin and two engineer accounts in each workspace (SAML group mapping for later).
- Issue one short-lived developer API token for dev + one immutable service account token for CI (rotated on our side every 30 days unless you prefer rotation control).
- Apply role mappings: Viewer / Developer / Admin per list attached.
- Configure prefix-based KV caching and a per-route rate limit for your initial integration endpoints.

I've attached an initial-access-checklist and a short policy note for service accounts. Can you confirm these names for the workspaces and the two engineers who should get dev access? Also tell us whether you want us to seed the CI service account token into your Azure Key Vault (we support direct KMS/HSM integrations) or hand over the token for you to inject.

Planned timeline: provisioning within 48 hours of names/confirmation; handoff call and live walkthrough the following day.

Next steps (ask):
1) Confirm engineer emails for seeding (dev env and prod admin).
2) Confirm preferred token handoff method (Redwood-managed rotation into your KMS, or manual).
3) Any compliance checklist items we should pre-attach (SOC2 evidence, IP allowlist ranges).

I can start the provisioning as soon as you reply; Marissa will coordinate invites and Monica will own the token exchange.

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Anthony Ruiz <anthony.ruiz@blueharbor.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Workspace provisioning & initial access plan — Blueharbor Analytics

Jonas,

This looks good — thanks. Quick answers:
- Use workspace names exactly as you proposed (blueharbor-dev, blueharbor-prod).
- Seed users: alex.mendoza@blueharbor.ai, priya.shah@blueharbor.ai (dev engineers); myself (anthony.ruiz@blueharbor.ai) as prod admin.
- For the CI service account token, we prefer Redwood to seed it into our Azure Key Vault. We'll provide a service principal with write permissions; let us know the principal id.
- Compliance: we need IP allowlisting for prod (our networking team will provide the CIDR blocks) and we'll need evidence of token rotation policy for the first 90 days.

Can we do the walkthrough at 3pm PT tomorrow?

Thanks,
Anthony

Subject: Re: Workspace provisioning & initial access plan — Blueharbor Analytics

Thanks Anthony — that works.

Action confirmations:
- Workspaces: blueharbor-dev / blueharbor-prod (confirmed).
- Seeded accounts: alex.mendoza@blueharbor.ai, priya.shah@blueharbor.ai, anthony.ruiz@blueharbor.ai.
- Azure Key Vault seeding for CI token: please send the service principal id and a writeable secret path. We'll use a short handshake token first to prove access, then push the CI token and rotate it once after initial validation.
- IP allowlist: we'll stub the firewall rules for prod and request your CIDR block prior to enabling.

Couple of implementation details so expectations are clear:
- Dev token: scoped to per-route generate and embedding endpoints only; TTL 24h. We'll provide a refresh flow sample you can embed in your dev tooling.
- CI token (service account): scoped to model-serving routes + read-only usage reporting; rotation managed via Redwood if you choose.
- SAML mappings: if you want SSO, we recommend mapping your SAML group names to Redwood roles now (e.g., redwood-admins, redwood-developers) — we can do a mapping pass on the kickoff.

I've attached: blueharbor-initial-access-checklist.xlsx (checklist + role matrix) and rbw-service-account-policy.txt (recommended token scoping and rotation cadence).

We'll provision dev workspace once Monica gets the service principal and Marissa gets your list for invites. Ben — can you take the lead on setting up the initial rate-limit + cache policy for blueharbor-dev?

Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

I'll schedule the 3pm PT walkthrough for tomorrow and send calendar invites in a minute. For the invite workflow:

- For your prod admin (anthony.ruiz), I'll send an admin invite with MFA enforcement and the role description we discussed.

Thanks — this looks good to us. A couple of clarifications before the walkthrough:

1) On the dev token TTL: 24h is fine, but can you provide a short endpoint example for programmatic refresh? Our SDK team prefers a refresh flow rather than issuing new personal tokens.
2) For the CI secret path in Key Vault: we'll use /secrets/blueharbor/ci/redwood. I will send the service principal id as a separate email from our infra team (security sends it).

Once we have the service principal and the invites, we are comfortable proceeding with the provisioning. Looking forward to the walkthrough at 3pm PT tomorrow.

Clara
Head of Platform Engineering
Blueharbor Analytics
